Lambson family · Person

Glenn Cody Lambson

1898–1934

Open in the family tree

Born
January 26, 1898 · Springville, Utah
Died
June 18, 1934 · Bingham Canyon, Utah
Burial
Mount Olivet Cemetery, Salt Lake City, Utah

Born in Springville and died in Bingham Canyon. Family-supplied newspaper citations report Army enlistment in May 1918 and list Private Glenn C. Lambson with Field Remount Squadron No. 309 in a July 1919 overseas-return report. The original notices, hometown discrepancy, and exact service dates still need review; France remains his sister Clara’s recollection.

Glenn Cody married Mary Lucille Jamieson on September 11, 1922, in Salt Lake City. Their children were Norma Lucille, Vera Elaine, and Glenn Jamieson. The family supplied citations to Army enlistment notices naming Glenn C. Lambson in two Salt Lake newspapers on May 9, 1918. A transcription from the Salt Lake Tribune of July 8, 1919, lists Private Glenn C. Lambson with Field Remount Squadron No. 309 among servicemen returning from overseas through New York. These contemporary reports add detail to the probable matching overseas-cavalry entry in the 1924 Utah military roster.

The newspaper citations and return-notice transcription were supplied by the archive owner; their scans have not yet been independently inspected. The return entry gives his hometown as “Springfield,” whereas Glenn’s birth and the 1924 roster identify Springville. Preserve that discrepancy until the original notice and a service record can be compared. May 9, 1918 is the enlistment notices’ publication date, not an independently established enlistment date; July 8, 1919 is the return article’s publication date, not a confirmed arrival or discharge date. The 1924 roster prints both enlistment and discharge as May 9, 1918; that unresolved anomaly must not be interpreted as one day of service or silently corrected. His sister Clara recalled service in France; the newspaper extract and roster do not independently establish France, an exact discharge date, or his identity through a full-name service record.
